Pink tax is crazy. If you’re looking for a simple period tracker, use a different app.

This app is incredibly cluttered with unnecessary features, constant buttons, and ads everywhere. Personally, I don’t need system tracking, fertility predictions, meditation, articles, or a dozen different tabs. I just want something that reliably tracks my cycle.

The ads are bad enough in itself but the pricing is really what rubbed me the wrong way. Women already deal with enough “pink tax” nonsense, and somehow a clunky period tracker wants $3.99/month, $24.99/year, or $69.99 for a lifetime subscription. But here’s the funny part: when I went to leave this review, I tapped “rate us” in the menu. if you select “yes, I like the app,” it sends you to the App Store to leave a review. If you select “no,” suddenly the “lifetime” subscription jobs from $69.99 to just $3.99. 

This in itself just gave me a nasty feeling. The developers clearly are just trying to get any dollar out of anyone who uses this app by any means possible. I personally don’t even think it’s worth $3. I don’t even leave reviews but this felt necessary to speak on.

After three years, I’m finally switching to another tracker. I never paid much attention to all the issues within this app because I only use it for 2 seconds every month. All of this became apparent to me once I began to transfer my data to another app and it seemed like an ad was popping up every couple seconds. I was shocked.

What should be a simple tool for tracking data feels more focused on pushing subscriptions and serving ads rather than providing a clean user experience. After three years, I’m done. Boo to the developers. 🍅🍅🍅
